criteria.evidence: Rules & behavior: "When the project itself now shows a different answer than the earlier one (for example a database it did not have), the proposal names the project as its source..." / "A run with every answer unchanged changes nothing." / Acceptance: "Given the product owner changes the database answer from no to yes...". The Agent intent says "Fails if: a re-run keeps a memory file or rule group that a changed answer rules out", and Outputs list "memory files added or taken out, rule groups now kept or skipped", but no rule says what happens at that branch.
criteria.fix: Add to Rules & behavior the two branches the guidance says this section must cover: (1) when a changed answer rules out something the first run built (for example the database answer goes from yes to no), the re-run takes the database standard out of the project's memory and marks the review's database rule group as skipped, and records both in the change record; (2) when the profile holds no earlier answers (the first run never finished), the run asks the questions as a first run does, with proposals from the project and Phoenix memory only, and says so. Add a matching Given/When/Then for branch (1): "Given the database answer changes from yes to no, when the run ends, then the database standard is no longer in the project's memory and the database rule group is recorded as skipped."

criteria.evidence: "The tracker rule holds on every run: nothing is made in the tracker before a typed yes." and "When the project itself now shows a different answer than the earlier one (for example a database it did not have), the proposal names the project as its source and the earlier answer is shown beside it. Our default; the sources do not say how a change is shown."
criteria.fix: Give each of these two lines its why. For the tracker line, add: "because the tracker is an outside system the whole team sees, and a re-run is as able to make a wrong type as a first run." For the project-shown-answer line, add why the project wins as the proposal and why the earlier answer stays beside it, for example: "because what the project holds now is newer evidence than an old answer, and showing the earlier answer beside it lets the product owner see what changed before confirming."

criteria.evidence: Every section is a list of discrete bullets; acceptance is in Given/When/Then ("Given a project that was initialized before, when the product owner runs `initialize` again, then each question proposes the earlier answer and names it as its source."); the feature states the function's behavior ("Lets the product owner run `initialize` again at any time..."), not a user story.

Parent capability gives one line: "Run initialize again (fn-rerun-initialize): lets the product owner run initialize again when the project changes, with the earlier answers proposed, so the set-up follows the project." The feature adds inputs and outputs ("Out: a record of what changed since the last run: answers changed, memory files added or taken out, rule groups now kept or skipped, tracker types made or mapped."), rules ("A run never removes a work-item type from the tracker. A type may hold work items the team still uses.") and four testable acceptance criteria.

What: "A second run reads the earlier answers and proposes each one again with the earlier answer as its source, so the product owner confirms what still holds and corrects only what changed." Why: "when the project changes: it gains a database, a web surface, personal data or a new tracker, or it drops one. The set-up then follows the project without a reinstall." Edges: "The first run's questions, memory, rule groups and tracker types (fn-setup-questions, fn-project-memory, fn-review-rule-groups and fn-881 own them; this feature reuses them)." / "Reinstalling Garura (the install play owns it)."
